speaker: Doctor
text: I need to assess your current vital signs immediately; have you been experiencing fever, rapid heart rate, or excessive sweating recently? Additionally, have you consumed any illicit substances or had a recent history of trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient's roommates report that he has been displaying increasingly aggressive and unusual behavior. They mention that he has been under significant stress due to final exams and has become more reclusive. Earlier this evening, he exhibited extreme irritability, yelled at his computer, broke it, and then spent several hours at the gym.

speaker: Doctor
text: That gym session sounds intense; did you notice any shaking, confusion, or blurred vision during or after your workout? Also, have you been taking any new medications, supplements, or substances like cocaine or methamphetamine recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive behavior and irritability. I also have Yelling, Breaking objects, Prolonged physical activity (several hours at the gym), Rapid speech during exam, Aggressiveness during exam. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous diagnosis of gastroenteritis does not fit your symptoms of aggression, prolonged exertion, and rapid speech; have you consumed any substances like amphetamines, cocaine, or excessive caffeine recently? I also need to know if you have any history of thyroid problems or diabetes. REQUEST TEST: TSH, Urine_Tox_Screen, Blood_Glucose, Electrolytes.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: TSH: Normal, Urine_Tox_Screen: Amphetamines Positive, Cocaine Negative, Opiates Negative, Benzodiazepines Negative, Cannabinoids Negative, Blood_Glucose: Normal, Electrolytes: Sodium Normal, Potassium Normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stimulant Induced Psychotic Disorder (Amphetamine Intoxication). The combination of urinary amphetamines, prolonged exertion, and acute aggression with normal glucose and thyroid levels confirms this diagnosis.
